proposals.old_step: 4.1 For $\Phi(\theta,\varphi)=a(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$, $0\le\theta\le\pi$, $0\le\varphi\le2\pi$, direct differentiation gives $|\Phi_\theta\times\Phi_\varphi|=a^2\sin\theta$. The poles and seam contribute zero to the surface integral, so $\operatorname{area}(S_a)=a^2\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi=4\pi a^2$. The parameter change $(\theta,\varphi)\mapsto(\pi-\theta,\varphi+\pi\bmod2\pi)$ preserves this density and induces the antipodal map. Thus the antipodal map $n\mapsto-n$ preserves spherical area and reverses $n$, so $\int_{S_a}n\,dS=0$. Integrating the expression in step 3.1 and using $\operatorname{area}(S_a)=4\pi a^2$ gives $\int_{S_a}\sigma n\,dS=(3\mu/(2a))4\pi a^2U=6\pi\mu aU$. [step 3.1, algebra]
proposals.proposed_step: 4.1 For any radius $a>0$, parameterize the sphere by $\Phi_a(\theta,\varphi)=a(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$ on $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$, using the admitted seam and pole boundary convention. Its parameter tangents have Gram coefficients $E=a^2$, $F=0$ and $G=a^2\sin^2\theta$, so the area density is $\sqrt{EG-F^2}=a^2\sin\theta$. The parameter boundary contributes zero to these integrals. Thus $\operatorname{Area}(S_a)=\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi a^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi=4\pi a^2$. The antipodal parameter map is $(\theta,\varphi)\mapsto(\pi-\theta,\varphi+\pi\ {\rm mod}\ 2\pi)$: split the longitude interval at $\pi$ so each part is an ordinary affine substitution. It has absolute Jacobian one, sends $\Phi_a$ to $-\Phi_a$, and preserves $a^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$ because $\sin(\pi-\theta)=\sin\theta$. Hence $n$ changes sign under an area-preserving substitution and $\int_{S_a}n\,dS=0$. Integrating the stress in step 3.1 gives $\int_{S_a}\sigma n\,dS=(3\mu/(2a))4\pi a^2U=6\pi\mu aU$. [F3, F4, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

facts_to_add.label: F4
facts_to_add.exact_source_excerpt: For a continuous scalar field $q$ on the patch image, $\int_Sq\,dS:=\int_D(q\circ\varphi)J_\varphi$, and $\operatorname{Area}(S):=\int_DJ_\varphi$.
facts_to_add.proposed_fact: [F4] [[def-surface-area-and-scalar-surface-integral-of-a-patch]]: integrate a continuous scalar field against the chart density on the parameter region; area is the integral of that density, and content-zero parameter boundaries do not change the value.

proposals.reason: The current result is sound, but the local proof assumes the chart-area evaluation/invariance without doing its density computation. The explicit Gram coefficients, sphere-area integral and split antipodal parameter substitution close exactly that omission without changing the public claim.

downstream_step_proposal.old: 5.1 On $r=R$ the integrand in step 2.2 is $O(R^{-3})$ and the area is $4\pi R^2$, so its integral tends to zero as $R\to\infty$. The left side is nonnegative and nondecreasing in $R$; since it equals a quantity tending to zero, it is zero for every $R>a$. Continuity then gives $\nabla w=0$ throughout the connected exterior, so $w$ is constant there; its far-field limit is zero, hence $w=0$. The equation now gives $\nabla q=0$, so $q$ is constant, and its zero far-field limit gives $q=0$. [step 2.2, algebra] ∎

proposals.old_step: 3.1 On the sphere, $u=(3/2)U_t$ with $U_t=U-(U\cdot n)n$, so $|u|^2=(9/4)(|U|^2-(U\cdot n)^2)$. Thus $p|_{r=a}$ depends on $n$ only through $(U\cdot n)^2$ and is unchanged by $n\mapsto-n$. The antipodal map preserves spherical area and reverses $n$, so the vector integrand $p n$ has zero integral over the sphere. By the stress convention in [F2], $\int_{|x|=a}\sigma_En\,dS=-\int_{|x|=a}pn\,dS=0$. [given, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

Thus $p|_{r=a}$ depends on $n$ only through $(U\cdot n)^2$ and is unchanged by $n\mapsto-n$. For any radius $a>0$, parameterize the sphere by $\Phi_a(\theta,\varphi)=a(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$ on $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$, using the admitted seam and pole boundary convention. Thus $\operatorname{Area}(S_a)=\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi a^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi=4\pi a^2$. The antipodal parameter map is $(\theta,\varphi)\mapsto(\pi-\theta,\varphi+\pi\ {\rm mod}\ 2\pi)$: split the longitude interval at $\pi$ so each part is an ordinary affine substitution. It has absolute Jacobian one, sends $\Phi_a$ to $-\Phi_a$, and preserves $a^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$ because $\sin(\pi-\theta)=\sin\theta$. Under this substitution $p$ is unchanged and $n$ reverses, hence $\int_{S_a}pn\,dS$ equals its own negative and is zero. By [F2], the formal resultant is $\int_{S_a}\sigma_E n\,dS=-\int_{S_a}pn\,dS=0$. [given, F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, construct, algebra] ∎
